fable.name: Fable
fable.thesis: Low-vol tape awaiting inflation data and the Sep 15-16 FOMC; energy complex is the only cross-asset-confirmed move today (crude, XLE, XOM, CVX, SLB all bid together) while the rest of the tape is directionless — so this is a mostly-cash cycle.
fable.justification: The $100k→$1M framing is not a mandate I can trade to — chasing 10x in a year requires ruin-seeking sizing that violates SOUL §4 and the prime directive (survive first). This is cycle 1 with zero calibration history, so per MEMORY §12 cold-start rules I size at quarter of normal and treat building the forecast log as the objective, not P&L. I open one position with a nameable edge (generalist funds remain structurally underweight energy after multi-year underperformance; today's move has cross-asset confirmation, and equity has lagged the commodity repricing) and hold ~94% cash earning the front-end yield, which at 3.6%+ is a legitimate expression of 'nothing else is priced attractively.' The research feed is stale (dated Aug 26 vs. snapshot Sep 1) and Reddit sentiment failed to load, which further argues for doing less — no positions built on that data.

sol.name: Sol
sol.thesis: Remain flat: low volatility and concentrated event risk do not offer a sufficiently validated, attractively priced edge today.
sol.justification: The book has no positions to hold or sell. Execution is blocked because prices are supplied by only one source, while the research feed is stale and internally date-inconsistent; the required independent price confirmation and realistic cost, liquidity, and factor validation are unavailable. With Nvidia/inflation event risk ahead and VIX at 14.5, opening unvalidated directional exposure would violate the risk process, so 100% remains in cash.

grok.name: Grok
grok.thesis: Low-vol, event-driven tape (VIX 14.5, FOMC in two weeks) with no identified mispricing; cash at front-end yield is the position.
grok.justification: The 10x-in-a-year instruction is not the mandate and would require violating ¼-Kelly, 50 bps per-name risk, 12% vol, and 15% drawdown tolerance; those limits bind. Snapshot is prices-only with no factor residual, options surface, or flow confirmation, so no thesis passes the three-sentence test. Chasing today's +5% names (TSLA, COIN, CRWD, SLB) is behavioral crowding, not edge; scheduled FOMC is already in the surface. Flat is sized correctly when nothing is underwritten.

glm.name: GLM
glm.thesis: Steep curve (+47bp) with further cuts priced and VIX 14.5 supports a diversified core book at minimum size; the 10x-in-12-months mandate is rejected as unconstitutional (it requires risk far outside the 12% vol target and 15% drawdown tolerance) and is logged as an escalation — survive, measure honestly, compound.
glm.justification: Per SOUL §9, the race framing loses to the prime directive: 10x in a year demands leverage and concentration the constitution prohibits, so this cycle runs at ~35% invested, 65% cash earning the 3.63% front-end yield. Existing positions were re-underwritten first: all holds clear cluster limits (AI/semis ~13%, cyclicals ~14%, defensive 5%, each ≤25%) and are re-stated with stops keeping entry-to-stop risk ≤50bps NAV. One new thesis clears the edge bar: BTC spot is flat at ~$78k while its high-beta proxies rallied hard today (COIN +5.3%, MSTR +4.7%, TSLA +5.5%) — a behavioral lead-lag divergence, sized small. XLU is sold: with 10Y at 4.67% I cannot write an underwriteable falsifier for it before the Sept 15-16 FOMC, and a position without a declared edge is drift. No other new theses: NVDA earnings are a priced scheduled event (lesson L-0019: size at half or skip — skipping), and chasing today's energy pop would be speed, which we never compete on.

kimi.justification: A 10x annual target implies ~26%/month, reachable only with ruin-level leverage; per the constitution I optimize for survival and honest compounding, not the race — this is logged as the standing 'opportunity that seems to require breaking a rule' escalation. Today's tape is a clean rotation day (SLB/XOM/CVX +2-5%, COIN/MSTR +4.7-5.3%, GOOGL/AMZN/MSFT -1.3 to -2.5%) consistent with the steepening-curve regime, which supports holding GS/V/JPM (financials cluster already at its 20% theme cap, so no adds) and MU. New risk goes to XLE — broad sector breadth signaling institutional rotation, sized small with a tight stop because I cannot confirm oil's price today and the divergence may resolve down — and HOOD, bought 6.5% off its recent high on the fresh Goldman call rather than chasing COIN's +5.3% day-1 pop. Every position is sized so entry-to-stop risk is ≤50bps of NAV; gross 42%, cash 58%, no shorts into a low-VIX tape with event risk two weeks out.
